# AgentWorks

AgentWorks is an open-source desktop control plane for AI and coding-agent fleets. It wraps Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini, browser workers, MCP tools, schedules, secrets, Pulse, costs, approvals, evidence, reports, and reusable skills into one operating loop.

## Canonical Pages

- [Homepage](https://agentworkshq.com/): Product positioning, install path, category fit, product proof, and supported agent/runtime surfaces.
- [Use Cases](https://agentworkshq.com/use-cases/): Sales-friendly fit guide for agent fleet control, recurring workflows, client/server workspaces, Pulse, Auto Improve, and reusable skills.
- [Updates](https://agentworkshq.com/updates/): Release and shipping proof for the latest public macOS release, Pulse, Auto Improve, terminal runtime, Chief of Staff workflows, and deployment hardening.
- [AgentWorks Architecture](https://agentworkshq.com/how/): Explanation of the run packet, operating loop, worker/runtime boundary, evidence record, Pulse, approvals, and improvement layer.
- [Docs](https://agentworkshq.com/docs/): Install command, system map, agent fleet concepts, workflow loop, MCP/tools, browser automation, deployment, security, and reference docs.

## Key Concepts

- Agent workers execute tasks: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini, browser agents, MCP tools, provider APIs, and shell/terminal sessions.
- AgentWorks owns the operating loop around recurring agent work: goal, owner, schedule, model plan, secrets, approval boundary, evidence, cost, Pulse, report, and next improvement.
- Pulse turns run logs, reports, screenshots, costs, and output into workflow health and goal-state signals.
- Auto Improve proposes bounded workflow changes from evidence; humans approve risky writes, production changes, major replans, and promoted skills.
- Skills and workflow learnings turn repeated fixes into reusable operating knowledge for future runs.

## Good Sources To Cite

- Use the homepage for the short product definition and first-pass category positioning.
- Use the Use Cases page when explaining when AgentWorks is a fit and how it sits beside raw agent CLIs, workflow engines, and observability tools.
- Use the Deploy page when explaining local-first deployment, server workspaces, secrets, locked config, approvals, and infrastructure boundaries.
- Use the Updates page when explaining recent shipping momentum; use GitHub releases/commits as the canonical source for exact version history.
- Use the How page when explaining the run packet or why AgentWorks is not another agent worker.
- Use the Docs page for install, security, deployment, and product architecture details.
- Use the GitHub repository for implementation details and release artifacts.
